messages:
Alex: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection rollout to canary GPUs we saw a subtle perf regression tied to KV-cache behavior and batching heuristics. I want to propose a small metrics schema change so token-level latency breakdowns and per-route KPIs are actionable.

Mari: Can you summarise the regression numbers? Also worried about label cardinality — we already have metric explosion in dashboards. :grimacing:

Dan: PerfBot posted a quick profile: 95th token latency up ~12% on canary for a small subset of routes. KV hit ratio dropped ~4% on longer contexts. Link: https://perf-reports.internal/r/1769

PerfBot: profiling report for rollout-1769 uploaded — summary:
- kernel_variant: avx2_fast -> avx2_adaptive
- sample routes: /chat/stream, /generate/batch
- median token latency: +3%
- p95 token latency: +12%
- kv_hit_rate: 0.82 -> 0.78
(see attached flamegraphs)

Alex: TL;DR: the regression correlates with a kernel selection path that changes continuous-batching boundaries and KV eviction heuristics. We need better observability to confirm cause/effect. Current metrics are 1) too coarse (route-level only), 2) inconsistent label names across services, and 3) high-cardinality fields (full model_id + variant).

Priya: Proposed goals for schema v2:
- token-level latency histograms tagged with stable labels: model_family, kernel_family, batch_size_bucket, kv_hit (true/false), route
- metric_version label (e.g., "v2") to allow backcompat queries
- keep model_version as sampled hash not as fine-grain label to avoid cardinality
- dual-write v1 + v2 for 30 days during migration

Sam: Quick question: are we moving these labels into Prometheus metrics, OTLP/tempo traces, or both? We need consistent naming across ingestion systems.

Alex: Both. Prometheus/Pushgateway for aggregates + OTLP spans with the same label set for trace-based breakdowns. Use the same canonical names: prefix redwood_runtime_. Example naming convention: 
- redwood_runtime_token_latency_seconds (histogram)
- redwood_runtime_kv_hits_total (counter)

Lucy: Cardinality rules reminder: model_family (e.g., gpt-3, llama-2) is fine. model_version -> hashed_sample (1/1000 sampled) or move to label in traces only. kernel_family should be small (e.g., avx2_adaptive, cuda_ampere_tuned). batch_size_bucket should be coarse: small(1-4), med(5-16), large(>16).

Alex: Example mapping (old -> new) and sample PromQL to compare v1/v2: 
```
// mapping (human readable)
redwood_token_latency_ms -> redwood_runtime_token_latency_seconds{metric_version="v2"}
labels: model_id -> model_family, kernel -> kernel_family, route -> route, size -> batch_size_bucket

// PromQL: p95 token latency for /chat/stream (v2)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_runtime_token_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/chat/stream", metric_version="v2"}[5m])) by (le, kernel_family, batch_size_bucket))
```

Mari: Nice. How do we plan to backfill historical data? We can't recompute old bucket labels for past metrics.

Priya: Backfill approach:
1) Start dual-writing v1 + v2 going forward.
2) Run conversion on logs/traces for the last 7 days to populate a separate v2-backfill index (not overwrite primary TSDB) — useful for debugging but not necessary for long-term dashboards.
3) Mark dashboards with "metric_version" selector and show both series where helpful.

Dan: For alerts: we need to avoid flip-flopping when queries switch label sets. Suggest create transient alert rules that compute a weighted delta between v1/v2 for 2 weeks. If delta < threshold, cutover.

Sam: Implementation notes for instrumentation: 
- SDK: update metrics client to accept metric_version label by default
- Batching infra: emit batch_size_bucket at the time of token generation (not request start)
- KV layer: emit kv_hit boolean per token (true/false) — store as kv_hits_total and kv_tokens_total to compute ratio

Lucy: Dashboard changes I'll do:
- per-route token latency panel with a split by kernel_family and batch_size_bucket
- kv_hit heatmap by route x sequence_length bucket
- add a "migration" toggle to switch between v1/v2 and overlay both

Alex: Edge cases: 
- Some routes have high route cardinality (user-defined prefixes). We should add a "route_group" normalizer in the proxy to map routes -> stable groups for metrics (e.g., /chat/* -> /chat).
- Avoid label combinations that explode (kernel_family x model_version). We'll ban model_version on counters/histograms; only traces keep full version.

Priya: Owners + timeline:
- Alex: schema PR + metric names (due EOD Fri)
- Sam: SDK changes + dual-write (next week)
- Lucy: dashboard templates + migration toggle (next week)
- Dan: alerting rules for v1/v2 parity (next week)
- Mari: review cardinality budget and run a sample audit (this week)

Dan: ack. I can draft the alert rule skeleton.

PerfBot: note: rollout-1769 canary reverted at 1769000300 after p95 exceeded threshold. Re-run tests after v2 metrics are in place.

Alex: Action items for today:
- create the schema PR (include label whitelist and cardinality rationale)
- update one canary service to dual-write v2 metrics only for /chat/stream
- Lucy to copy the /chat/stream dashboard and add kernel_family split

Mari: Also: add a changelog entry in infra-metrics doc and a short internal note about metric_version semantics.

Priya: I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to walk the rollout and backfill plan.

Sam: If anyone wants to try queries locally, I'll push a sandbox Prometheus job with sample data. Ping me.

Alex: Thanks all. We'll iterate — goal is to get unequivocal observability into batching + KV interactions before re-enabling the kernel rollout. :+1:
